e-144.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = 2x^3 - 2x$ at the point $(1,0).$
e-144.worked_solution:
Let $f(x) = 2x^3 - 2x.$ Computing the derivative $f'(x)$ gives

$$
f'(x)  = 6x^2-2.
$$

We then compute $f'(1)$, which gives

$$
f'(1)  = 6(1)^2-2 = 4.
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=4$ and the coordinates of our point $(1,0),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =4(x-1) \\ y & =4x-4.\end{aligned}
$$

e-146.knowledge_point: Determining where a Tangent Line Intersects an Axis
e-146.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y=4\sqrt{x}+4x$ at the point $(1,8)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
e-146.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4\sqrt{x}+4x.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\sqrt{x}+4x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{1/2}+4x) \\  & =2{x}^{-1/2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
m=f'(1) = 2(1)^{-1/2}+4 = 6.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-8 & =6(x-1) \\ y & =6x-6+8 \\ y & =6x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =6x+2 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $\left(-\dfrac 1 3, 0\right).$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y={x}^{2}-6x$ at the point $(3,-9).$
after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{2}-6x.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-6x)=2x-6.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(3)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3)=2(3)-6=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=0$ and the coordinates of our point $(3,-9),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-9) & =0(x-3) \\ y & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1)=10(1)+4=14\,.\end{aligned}

$$

content.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=5{x}^{2}+4x$ at the point $(1,9).$
content.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=5{x}^{2}+4x.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{2}+4x)=10x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1)=10(1)+4=14\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=14$ and the coordinates of our point $(1,9),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(9) & =14(x-1) \\ y & =14x-14+9 \\ y & =14x-5.\end{aligned}
$$
